Test results — every hardware run, with its result and its source

What has run on silicon, on which part and toolchain, and what it returned. Each row cites the DECISIONS.md entry that recorded the run. That log is the primary record; this document is an index into it and adds no result of its own.

For what has not run, read PROJECT_PLAN.md §"Test coverage gaps". The two documents are complements: this one lists runs, that one lists the suites no run has covered.

How to read this

"Pass" means both halves were captured. From D113 onward an entry says "green" only when the secure and non-secure suites both completed with zero failures and both logs were read back. Where only one half was captured, the cell says so rather than reading "pass". Three cells carry that qualification, and §7 lists them.

Suite counts differ between eras, because the trees differ. The isolation-1 regression trees report 14 or 15 suites (D067, D072); the isolation-2 and isolation-3 trees report secure 9/9 and non-secure 7/7 (D113 onward). A changed count is not a changed result.

PSA Arch tallies read pass / fail / skip.

Build-tree names

Entries cite trees by short name. They live in C:\b, 67 of them, and are not in this repository. The name is positional:

SegmentMeaning

g, iGNUARM, IAR
l1i, l2, l3isolation 1 with the IPC backend, isolation 2, isolation 3
flih, slihthe FF-M interrupt handling model under test
cry, att, stothe PSA Arch suite: crypto, attestation, storage

So m5il3 is RA6M5 under IAR at isolation 3, and m2gl2ns is the non-secure half of RA8M2 under GNUARM at isolation 2. There is no m5il1i or m2il1i: no IAR tree exists at isolation 1 with IPC (D124).

D067 also recorded two suites that report PASSED without testing anything. Do not read either as coverage:

  • TFM_S_CRYPTO_TEST_1056 / TFM_NS_CRYPTO_TEST_1056 (ECDSA-SECP384R1-SHA384) self-skip on every platform that is not Arm CryptoCell, because the gate tests CC3XX_RUNTIME_ENABLED. PSA_WANT_ECC_SECP_R1_384 is not disabled here, so **P-384 is untested on this port and probably works.** It needs a standalone check before anyone claims P-384 support.
  • TFM_S_CRYPTO_TEST_1045 / TFM_NS_CRYPTO_TEST_1044 (deterministic ECDSA) report a partial pass by design. sce9/crypto_accelerator_config.h:34 undefines PSA_WANT_ALG_DETERMINISTIC_ECDSA because SCE9 has no RFC 6979 path. Verification did run.

2. PSA Arch suites

All of these ran at profile_large, isolation 3, with the IPC backend.

The tree was the psa-arch-tests fork at tag renesas-ra-tfm-2.2.0, which carries the renesas_ra target and tf-m-tests' ten fetch_repo patches. An unpatched tree fails psa_verify_hash check 13 on any platform, so a run against one is not comparable to these (D014). GETTING_STARTED.md §3 has the clone.

SuiteRA6M5 GCCRA6M5 IARRA8M2 GCCRA8M2 IAR
crypto (64 tests)63 / 0 / 1 (D046)63 / 0 / 1 (D046)62 / 1 / 1 (D097, D099)62 / 1 / 1 (D104)
attestation1 / 0 / 0 (D046)1 / 0 / 0 (D046)1 / 0 / 0 — see §71 / 0 / 0 (D105)
storage, ITS + PS (17 tests)11 / 0 / 6 (D046)11 / 0 / 6 (D046)11 / 0 / 6 (D097)11 / 0 / 6 (D105)

Read "isolation 3" narrowly here. It says the SPM was configured at level 3, not that level-3 isolation was enforced. The shared isolation HAL compiled with TFM_ISOLATION_LEVEL undefined until D113, so none of these runs exercised the level-3 MPU table. The first runs that do are D114 and D123.

TFM_NS_IRQ_TEST_FLIH_1101 and _1102 are included in every §1 cell that reads "pass".

SLIH has never run on RA8M2 on either toolchain. The m2gslih and m2gslihns trees were built and never got a launch (D102, D126 §4). SLIH has also never run above isolation 1 on any part: the only SLIH launches are RA6M5's two at L1, ra6m5_TFM_slih_{gcc,iar}.launch. The SLIH service declares the same mmio_region as FLIH, so the region is exercised — but not through the SLIH path above L1.

D126 §4 corrected D116 and D119 on this point. Their claim that "RA8M2 is complete: every level this port supports" holds only for the regression-plus-FLIH configuration.

4. MCUboot upgrade path

Only RA8M2 has run this path. D100 was the first execution on any part in the port.

RunDateResultEntry
ra8m2_TFM_update_gcc2026-10-08both images install from their secondary slots; a second reset reports Swap type: none, so the secondary is erased and there is no re-installD100
ra8m2_TFM_update_iar2026-10-09install confirmed from rsp.br_hdr: ih_ver 2.3.0 at br_image_off 0x68000, which the launch had flashed at 2.2.0D106

The IAR evidence covers the install only. The second boot reporting Swap type: none was not observed under IAR; D100 proved the erase half on GCC through the same bootutil code (D106).

Neither other part has run it. RA6M5 has no *_TFM_update launch. RA6E1 set MCUBOOT_ALIGN_VAL to 128 to match its 128-byte code-flash write unit on 2026-08-29, and RA6E1_SOLUTION.md records that fix as not yet exercised on hardware: it only takes effect once BL2 writes code flash, which is an upgrade. **Images signed at one alignment are rejected by a BL2 built at another, because the trailer magic differs — reflash every slot and do not mix.**

Slot order is reversed for image 0 on RA8M2. The secure secondary at 0x02020000 sits below the secure primary at 0x02068000, so rsp.br_image_off = 0x68000 is the primary. Image 1 is the usual way round (D100).

5. Measured boot

A passing attestation suite proves nothing about measured boot. With component_cnt == 0 under the default ATTEST_TOKEN_PROFILE_PSA_IOT_1, attest_add_all_sw_components() emits IAT_NO_SW_COMPONENTS and returns success (D080). Every result below was obtained by reading the boot record, not by inferring it from a 1/0/0 attestation pass.

RA6E1 is the part RA6M5 and RA8M2 are derived from. It carries milestones M1 to M3 and is not re-run against the current build.

D015 states its own limit: the transcript has RTT dropouts and no end-of-suite summary was captured, so "no failure appeared" is not a certified clean sweep. It is the evidence that validated PLATFORM_HAS_ISOLATION_L3_SUPPORT, which D008 had declared on a build and a static region count alone.

RA6E1 is built with the D121 tfm_spm move and will not be run against it (D124).

7. Where the wording outruns the evidence

Four places. Each is recorded in the log itself; none is a new finding here.

ClaimWhat the evidence actually isSource
D122's RA6M5 L2 and L1+IPC cells read "green"both captures are secure 9/9 with the non-secure half truncated. Every entry from D113 onward means secure and non-secure by "green", so these two rows should read secure-onlyD125 §4
D123 §2's RA6M5 IAR L2 cellnon-secure 7/7 was captured; the secure suite "also passed" but its RTT output was not captured, so the secure half is reported rather than recorded. D123 says so itselfD128 §4
D115 §1's RA8M2 L3 secure half"the secure suite passed as far as the captured log runs". The non-secure half was captured separately and cleanlyD115 §1, D116 §3
RA8M2 GCC PSA Arch attestation, 1 / 0 / 0the figure appears in D106's M5 table and in RA8M2_SOLUTION.md, in both cases without a citation. No entry records that run. D096 confirms the attestation launch did boot m2cry / m2att on RA8M2 GCC, so the run happened; its tally has no entry behind itD106, D096

An RTT capture can truncate silently, and it looks like a hang

D072 worked out the tell, and it is worth reusing before anyone reports a failure:

  • Output stops after a result line and the next test is never announced — suspect the capture.
  • Output stops after a Description: line — suspect the target, and the named test is where to look.

A target that hangs inside a test prints that test's header first, because the framework emits it before the body runs. The non-secure RTT up-buffer is 4 KB against roughly 15 KB of log, which is why the capture is the likelier suspect. The first IAR SLIH run looked like a hang and was not: re-running the same binaries completed normally (D072).

8. One coverage note that no suite can reach

mbedtls_aes_crypt_ctr() in FSP 6.7's aes_alt.c ignores nc_off and stream_block and mishandles partial blocks. PSA Arch 236 and 237 pass on both parts, short-input CTR checks included, because the PSA cipher layer never reaches that function with a partial block. No suite in this matrix can see the defect, and a direct Mbed TLS CTR caller still hits it. Closing it needs a unit test against mbedtls_aes_crypt_ctr() itself, not another PSA-level suite (D099).
